Resolves #17963

Dock header actions now read as pane chrome instead of standalone buttons: compact transparent glyph controls use four-theme hover/active values, inline headers gain subtle neo-theme gradients with explicit classic-theme `none`, and Workstation opts into close, pin, and maximize as the living public witness. The existing Workstation overflow assertions now describe the merged #17960 contract: overflow is the first header action, close is last, and only the menu is body-mounted.

Evidence: L3 (local Chrome four-theme screenshots + Workstation Neural-Link action/overflow/theme path) → L3 required (AC1–AC5 browser-rendered visual and geometry behavior). Residual: AC4's retained full-tour `blankFrames` oracle reproduces open #17871 after every new action/order/overflow assertion passes; Residual-Owner: #17871.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Proof |
|---|---|
| AC-1 — compact glyph-first chrome in four themes | `ContainerUi.spec.mjs` renders and screenshots all four themes; 6/6 focused component arms green; screenshots visually inspected. |
| AC-2 — ordinary toolbars unchanged | The same browser fixture carries an ordinary `.neo-toolbar .neo-toolbar-action` negative control and proves its stock non-zero padding survives; the production selector requires the tab-header ancestor. |
| AC-3 — neo gradients, explicit classic `none` | All four `tab/Container.scss` value sheets declare the hook; computed-style assertions prove gradients only in the two neo themes, consumer override, and no leak into `ui:null`. |
| AC-4 — Workstation enables close, pin, maximize without a second overflow owner | Workstation sets all three inherited configs. The Neural-Link witness proves overflow first / close last / one owner and the menu/theme route; its independent retained pooled-grid oracle remains #17871. |
| AC-5 — gated state stays quiet without geometry shift | Each theme measures the hidden pin action's box, focuses the pane, and requires the exposed box to be identical before inspecting paint. |

## Deltas from ticket

- The final action boxes are 20px in classic themes and 24px in neo themes. A 32px neo draft produced a second Workstation overflow owner at the narrow desktop floor; the 24px arm restores the single-owner invariant while remaining visibly legible.
- The existing Workstation witness still asserted the pre-#17960 body-mounted control. It now binds the shipped contribution contract instead: control inside its source toolbar, menu on `document.body`.
- No action semantics, ordering implementation, dock model, or private consumer code changed.

## Test Evidence

Outside-CI receipts:

- `npm run build-themes -- -n -e all` — exit 0.
- `npx playwright test -c test/playwright/playwright.config.component.mjs test/playwright/component/tab/ContainerUi.spec.mjs` — 6/6 green in host Chrome after out-of-sandbox launch approval.
- HTML-reporter screenshots for all four themes were inspected; the controls remain monochrome at rest with small hover affordances, neo bands are subtle, and classic bands remain flat.
- Specificity mutant: the first neo-light arm rendered 48×32 because its theme-level button minimum tied the selector; strengthening the real dual toolbar class made all four square.
- Density mutant: 32px neo actions produced two Workstation overflow owners; 24px restores one.
- `WorkstationNL.spec.mjs` overflow/theme test — green. The full tour passes every new action/order/overflow assertion, then reproduces #17871's exact `rowsTop ≈ -2.5Mpx / visibleRows: 0` retained oracle.

## Post-Merge Validation

None — the visual, geometry, theme-switch, and Workstation integration effects are pre-merge observable.

## Evolution

The browser witnesses changed two design details before handoff: a specificity tie unique to neo-light required the toolbar's real dual base-class selector, and full-size 32px controls consumed enough header width to create a second overflow owner. The final 20px/24px density is therefore measured integration behavior, not an aesthetic guess.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge:** The chrome binds as `&.neo-toolbar > .neo-toolbar-action.neo-button` — a **direct-child** rule — while the ledger specifies the descendant form `.neo-tab-header-toolbar .neo-toolbar-action`. Today that is a distinction without a difference, because toolbar items are direct children and `#17960`'s overflow contribution lands as one. But the narrowing is now load-bearing and invisible: the first header action that is ever nested one level deeper — a grouped or wrapped contribution, an action inside a sub-container — silently renders as a stock button, and it will look like a theme bug rather than a selector-scope bug. The direct-child scope is doing real work (it is part of what wins the neo-light specificity tie), so I am not asking you to widen it. I am asking that the SCSS comment say *direct children only, and why*, because the comment currently explains the `.neo-toolbar` half of the negative contract but not the `>` half.

**Falsifications I ran that came back negative** — recorded so nobody re-derives them:

1. **Fifth theme.** `resources/scss/theme-cyberpunk` exists and the PR touches only four sheets, and the structural rule uses `var(--tab-header-action-size)` with **no fallback** — so an uncovered theme would collapse the actions to intrinsic glyph size with no hover affordance. Negative: `resources/scss/theme-cyberpunk/tab/` does not exist at all. Cyberpunk is a 13-file partial overlay (Global/button/container/dashboard/grid/toolbar) against theme-dark's 77, and defines *no* tab variables — not `--tab-container-content-border`, not the button metrics. Adding action values there would be the inconsistency. Four sheets is the established convention for tab variables and this PR follows it.
2. **Vacuous gated-box assertion.** `expect(exposedBox).toEqual(gatedBox)` would pass trivially if both were `null`. Negative for the current tree: `resources/scss/src/toolbar/Base.scss:14` gates with `pointer-events: none; visibility: hidden` — not `display: none` — so both boxes are real rects. It is also backstopped by `toHaveClass` before and `toBeVisible` after, which are not vacuity-capable. See suggestion S2 for the one line that would pin it.

- **S1 — colon alignment, 8 lines.** Measured rather than eyeballed: in all four theme sheets the two `--tab-header-action-background-color-active` / `-hover` declarations put their colon at column 50 while every sibling declaration in the same block — including the pre-existing `--tab-container-content-border` and your own seven other new lines — sits at column 51. Lint has no opinion, but this file family aligns religiously and the next person to add a variable will copy whichever neighbour they land on.
- **S2 — pin the gated-box arm against future vacuity.** `expect(exposedBox).toEqual(gatedBox)` names the property "focus gating preserves the action box", but if the gating carrier ever moves from `visibility: hidden` to `display: none`, both boxes become `null`, `toEqual` passes, and the assertion goes on reporting green while testing nothing. One line above it — `expect(gatedBox).not.toBeNull()` — makes the test fail loudly at the moment its premise dies instead of silently outliving it.
- **S3 — AC-2 says "byte-identically"; the arm proves one property.** `expect(ordinaryChrome.padding).not.toBe('0px')` does correctly discriminate the leak the AC cares about, so the scope guard is real. But two gaps sit under the word "byte-identical": it asserts one of the nine properties `readActionChrome` already collects, and `'0px'` is not the only thing a non-loading `button/Base.css` produces — a bare `<button>` inherits UA padding of `1px 6px`, so that arm would also pass if the stylesheet never loaded. You already capture the full `ordinaryChrome` object into the attachment; asserting it against a same-theme reference measured outside any tab header would close both gaps at once. The PR body's "proves its stock non-zero padding survives" is a touch stronger than what the assertion establishes — it proves the padding is non-zero, not that it is stock.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Documented searches — three things I tried to falsify and could not:**

1. **A vacuous selector.** `.neo-toolbar-action` must actually be emitted or the whole sheet is decoration. It is: `src/toolbar/Base.mjs:373` — `NeoArray.add(cls, 'neo-toolbar-action')`. The gated variant the spec asserts (`neo-toolbar-action-context-inactive`) is emitted at `:232`.
2. **Inert theme declarations.** This is the failure I missed reviewing #17956, where four classic-theme values silently duplicated the theme's own defaults. Not the case here: `--tab-header-action-*` is a NEW token family, consumed by the structural sheet with no prior definition, so every theme declaration changes a computed value. The classic/neo split is real too — 20px/2px vs 24px/4px, and semantic tokens rather than literals on the neo side.
3. **A negative control that cannot fail.** It asserts absence of the new rule's own signature properties on an ordinary action root. Planting that root in page-realm DOM rather than constructing a second Toolbar is deliberate and correct: the property under test is selector scope, and a second construction path would have tested the wrong thing.

**Challenge — one observation, explicitly NOT a finding against this PR:** the theme census is **five**, not four. `theme-cyberpunk` is absent from the diff, defines none of these tokens, and does not extend another theme (`Global.scss` only `@use`s `../motion`). Under it the new declarations resolve to invalid values and the actions lose size, radius and glyph colour.

I checked whether that is a regression this PR introduces, and it is not: `theme-cyberpunk` has **no `tab/` directory at all**, so tab chrome there is already unstyled — and the fallback-free consumption matches the house convention overwhelmingly (**54** fallback-free `var(--tab-*)` reads in `resources/scss/src/tab/` against **1** with a fallback, that one being #17956's `--tab-header-inline-background-image, none`). So this follows the established pattern rather than departing from it. Worth knowing only if cyberpunk is considered supported for dock surfaces; if it is, that is a sweep item for #17963, not a change here.
